title: Ask why
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What would happen if you asked 'why' five times about your own product?

A student said: when one of the engineers came in, he kept asking why about the product, and they kept simplifying it until they had a super streamlined product that was a lot cheaper. It doesn't take as much as you think to get from A to B. It is paralysis by over-analysis: you over-complicate systems and solutions.
I said: very good. He is relentless about asking questions and getting it done.

What about this man vibes with the person in the book? I said: he is relaxed, goes with the flow, open-minded. He said, in effect: this man is crazy and he's going to lose all his money, but he seems smart and motivated, and I like his style. He is a risk-taker.

He questions all the requirements and the rules and goes to the fundamentals of physics, I said. When you are building a culture, you have to study: what kind of person do I want, what is their level of risk, what will they tolerate?
In a startup like ours we have to attract that kind of risk-taker, the person who thinks outside the box, and who is relentless in asking questions and getting it done, I said.
A student said: I took some notes on things I can bring to the businesses I'm working with: asking the right questions.
What question have you not asked about your own product?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write your product and ask why of every part.
Write what you could remove to make it cheaper and simpler.
Write the risk level of the person you want.
Write the rule you would question first.
Write the kind of person you will attract.

check.q: What did the engineer in the student's story keep asking?
What did the student call over-complicating systems?
What did I say you have to study when building a culture?
choices: What kind of person you want and their level of risk

recap: Ask why until it is simple. Attract the risk-taker who asks questions.
